study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Jalbrzikowski et al., American Journal of Psychiatry, 2019
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Age-Associated Deviations of Amygdala Functional Connectivity in Youths With Psychosis Spectrum Disorders: Relevance to Psychotic Symptoms

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used four cohorts: Luna 1 and Luna 2 (University of Pittsburgh longitudinal and cross-sectional cohorts), Philadelphia Neurodevelopmental Cohort (PNC, University of Pennsylvania), and Pitt (University of Pittsburgh Conte Center study). PNC is a named public dataset; the other three are institutional cohorts from multiple sites, collectively representing MULTI-SITE (N>=2).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "The final neuroimaging data set consisted of 1,062 participants 10-25 years old (typically developing control subjects, N=622; individuals with psychosis spectrum disorders, N=194; individuals with other psychopathology, N=246) from four different samples. Three data sets were acquired at the University of Pittsburgh and one at the University of Pennsylvania."

answer.Luna 1: normative model training/testing (typically developing controls only)

answer.Luna 2: normative model training/testing (typically developing controls only)

answer.PNC: normative model training/testing (typically developing controls); clinical application (psychosis spectrum and other psychopathology groups)

answer.Pitt: normative model training/testing (typically developing controls); clinical application (psychosis spectrum group)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Luna 1 (N=213 TD) and Luna 2 (N=88 TD) provided only typically developing controls for normative model construction. PNC provided 292 TD for normative model and 162 psychosis spectrum + 246 other psychopathology for clinical comparison. Pitt provided 29 TD for normative model and 32 psychosis spectrum for clinical comparison.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Resting-state functional neuroimaging data from four samples (three cross-sectional, one longitudinal) were collected for 1,062 participants 10-25 years of age (622 typically developing control youths, 194 youths with psychosis spectrum disorders, and 246 youths with other psychopathology)."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Jalbrzikowski2019.pdf.md: Methods / Participants, L33-35; Table 1, L51-62

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was developed using 622 typically developing control youths from four cohorts (Luna 1: 213, Luna 2: 88, PNC: 292, Pitt: 29). The study does not explicitly report separate train/test splits for the normative model construction.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "The final neuroimaging data set consisted of 1,062 participants 10-25 years old (typically developing control subjects, N=622...)" and Table 1 showing Luna 1 (N=213), Luna 2 (N=88), PNC (N=292), Pitt (N=29) for typically developing group.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Jalbrzikowski2019.pdf.md: Methods / Participants, L33-35; Table 1, L51-62

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Weighted mean calculated from cohort-specific means: (213×16.7 + 88×19.5 + 292×16.2 + 29×21.0)/622 = 17.06 years. Pooled SD calculated using pooled variance formula: sqrt([(212×9) + (87×12.96) + (291×11.56) + (28×7.29)]/618) = 3.27 years. Age range 10-25 years is stated explicitly. No separate train phase reported.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: Table 1 shows: Luna 1 (N=213, Mean=16.7, SD=3.0, range 10-25), Luna 2 (N=88, Mean=19.5, SD=3.6, range 14-25), PNC (N=292, Mean=16.2, SD=3.4, range 10-22), Pitt (N=29, Mean=21.0, SD=2.7, range 12-25).

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Male total: 113 (Luna 1) + 45 (Luna 2) + 151 (PNC) + 18 (Pitt) = 327. Female total: 100 (Luna 1) + 43 (Luna 2) + 141 (PNC) + 11 (Pitt) = 295. Total = 622. Male percentage: 327/622 = 52.6%. Female percentage: 295/622 = 47.4%. No separate train phase reported.
dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: Table 1 shows Male/Female (N/N) for typically developing group: Luna 1 (113/100), Luna 2 (45/43), PNC (151/141), Pitt (18/11).
